question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
With hard work, commitment / and proper guidance, / Sivaram has become / a IPS officer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a IPS officer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sentence should read: "...Sivaram has become an IPS officer."

• Rule — Use of "a" and "an": The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound with which the following word begins, not its spelling. "An" is used before words beginning with a vowel sound, and "a" is used before words beginning with a consonant sound.

• The letter "I" in the abbreviation "IPS" is pronounced as /aɪ/ (like the word "eye"), which is a vowel sound. Therefore, the article "an" must be used before "IPS", not "a".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "With hard work, commitment" is grammatically correct as the opening part of the sentence.

• Option 2: "and proper guidance," is grammatically correct and correctly continues the list joined by "and".

• Option 4: "Sivaram has become" is grammatically correct — the Present Perfect tense is correctly used here.

NOTE

• The article used before an abbreviation/acronym depends on how its first letter is pronounced, not how it is spelled: e.g., an MLA (M is pronounced "em"), an SMS (S is pronounced "es"), but a UN official (U is pronounced "you", a consonant sound).

• Similarly: an hour, an honest man (silent "h") but a university, a European (the "u"/"eu" here sounds like "you", a consonant sound).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
A owl is a bird which has wide eyes, asymmetrical ears and is found mostly in forests.
option_1: and is found mostly in forests.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A owl is a bird.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sentence should read: "An owl is a bird which has wide eyes..."

• Rule — Use of "a" and "an": "An" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, while "a" is used before words that begin with a consonant sound.

• The word "owl" begins with the vowel sound /aʊ/. Therefore, the article "an" must be used before it, not "a".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "and is found mostly in forests." is grammatically correct and correctly completes the list of the owl's features.

• Option 2: "asymmetrical ears" is grammatically correct as a noun phrase describing a feature of the owl.

• Option 4: "which has wide eyes," is grammatically correct — the relative pronoun "which" correctly introduces a relative clause describing "owl".

NOTE

• Other commonly confused "a/an" words in SSC exams: an hour, an heir, an MBA, an X-ray (vowel sound) versus a university, a one-rupee note, a European (consonant sound "y"/"w" despite a vowel letter).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
The teacher will never / give you punishment / if you will / come on time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. if you will.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sentence should read: "The teacher will never give you punishment if you come on time."

• Rule — Conditional Sentences (Type 1): In a Type 1 (real/future) conditional sentence, the structure is: If + Subject + Present Simple, Subject + will + V1. The "if-clause" never takes "will" or any other future-tense marker, even though the idea being expressed is future in nature.

• Here, the main clause "The teacher will never give you punishment" already carries the future auxiliary "will". The subordinate if-clause "if you will come on time" wrongly repeats "will"; it should simply be "if you come on time".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "give you punishment" is grammatically correct as the object phrase of the main clause.

• Option 3: "come on time" is grammatically correct once "will" is removed from the if-clause preceding it.

• Option 4: "the teacher will never" is grammatically correct — the main clause correctly uses "will" for the future.

NOTE

• The rule "no will/would in the if-clause" applies to Type 1 and Type 2 conditionals alike (Type 2: If + Past Simple, ... would + V1).

• Exception: "will/would" can appear in an if-clause only when it expresses willingness/request, e.g., "If you will just wait a moment, I'll call him" (here "will" means "are willing to").

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
If she exercises daily, / she would / remain energetic / and fit forever.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. she would.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sentence should read: "If she exercises daily, she will remain energetic and fit forever."

• Rule — Conditional Sentences (Type 1): The if-clause "If she exercises daily" uses the Present Simple tense, which signals a Type 1 (real/likely) conditional. Its main clause must therefore use "will" + V1, not "would".

• "Would" belongs to the Type 2 (hypothetical/unreal) conditional, whose if-clause takes the Past Simple (e.g., "If she exercised daily, she would remain..."). Mixing a Present Simple if-clause with a "would" main clause is grammatically inconsistent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "remain energetic" is grammatically correct as the base-form verb phrase following "will"/"would".

• Option 2: "If she exercises daily," is grammatically correct — Present Simple is correctly used in a Type 1 if-clause.

• Option 3: "and fit forever" is grammatically correct as the continuation of the complement "energetic and fit forever".

NOTE

• Quick memory rule for conditionals: Type 1 → if + present, ... will; Type 2 → if + past, ... would; Type 3 → if + past perfect, ... would have + V3.

• A common SSC trap is exactly this kind of "tense-mismatch" between the if-clause and the main clause — always check that both clauses belong to the same conditional type.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Romantic poetry is a literary movement that emerged in the late 18th century and continued through the mid-19th century. It is (1)________ by an emphasis on emotion, imagination and individualism. Romantic poets sought to express their innermost thoughts and feelings through their poetry, often exploring (2)_______ such as love, beauty and mortality. One of the defining features of Romantic poetry is its use of language and imagery to evoke powerful emotions in the reader. Many Romantic poets, such as William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge (3)_________ that poetry should be written in the language of common people, rather than in the lofty, formal language of the past. They also incorporated vivid descriptions of nature and the natural world into their poetry, using it as a source of inspiration and spiritual renewal. (4)______ important aspect of Romantic poetry is its focus on the individual and the subjective experience. Romantic poets believed that each persons experience of the world was unique and valuable, and sought to capture this individuality in their writing. This led to a greater emphasis on personal expression and introspection in poetry, (5)_______ a rejection of the traditional poetic forms and structures of the past.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. characterised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "It is characterised by an emphasis on emotion, imagination and individualism." The passive structure "is/was + characterised by" is the standard idiomatic way of saying that something is "marked by" or "typified by" certain features.

• Rule: After the auxiliary verb "is", a past participle (V3) is required to form the passive voice, not a present-tense verb, an adjective, or a present-participle/gerund form.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "characterises" is the present-tense (V1/V5) form and cannot follow "is" to form the passive; "is characterises" is grammatically impossible.

• Option 2: "characteristic" is an adjective/noun ("a characteristic feature"), not a verb form, so it cannot combine with "by" to show agency in this way.

• Option 4: "characterising" is the present participle/gerund; "is characterising by" is not a valid passive construction (it would need to be "is characterised by").

NOTE

• Passive voice formula: Subject + is/am/are/was/were + V3 + by + Agent.

• Common SSC confusion pairs: "characterise/characterised", "involve/involved", "base/based" — always check whether the sentence needs the base verb, the past participle, or the adjective form.

Romantic poets sought to express their innermost thoughts and feelings through their poetry, often exploring (2)_______ such as love, beauty and mortality. One of the defining features of Romantic poetry is its use of language and imagery to evoke powerful emotions in the reader. Many Romantic poets, such as William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge (3)_________ that poetry should be written in the language of common people, rather than in the lofty, formal language of the past. They also incorporated vivid descriptions of nature and the natural world into their poetry, using it as a source of inspiration and spiritual renewal. (4)______ important aspect of Romantic poetry is its focus on the individual and the subjective experience. Romantic poets believed that each persons experience of the world was unique and valuable, and sought to capture this individuality in their writing. This led to a greater emphasis on personal expression and introspection in poetry, (5)_______ a rejection of the traditional poetic forms and structures of the past.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. themes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...often exploring themes such as love, beauty and mortality." Love, beauty and mortality are recurring subject matters explored in literature — the standard term for such recurring subject matters in a literary work is "themes".

• Rule — Word choice by context (Literary vocabulary): In literary/academic writing, ideas like love, beauty, and mortality that a poet repeatedly explores are called "themes", not "concerns", "arguments" or "problems", which carry different shades of meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "concerns" would suggest worries or matters of interest, which does not fit the literary context of "exploring" a subject in poetry as naturally as "themes".

• Option 2: "arguments" refers to reasoned points made to persuade, which is inappropriate here since love, beauty and mortality are not "arguments".

• Option 3: "problems" implies difficulties to be solved, which does not match the poetic, reflective sense intended in the sentence.

NOTE

• In literary analysis, remember the distinction: "theme" = the central idea/subject explored in a work; "motif" = a recurring element/image; "plot" = the sequence of events. SSC comprehension passages on literature often test this exact vocabulary.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. believed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Many Romantic poets, such as William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge believed that poetry should be written in the language of common people..."

• Rule — Tense consistency: The passage is written throughout in the Past Simple tense (e.g., "emerged", "sought", "incorporated", "believed") because it describes a historical literary movement. The verb filling this blank must therefore also be in the Past Simple tense to remain consistent with the surrounding narrative.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "could believe" wrongly introduces the modal "could", which changes the meaning to ability/possibility and breaks the factual, narrative tone of the passage.

• Option 2: "will believe" is future tense, which is inconsistent with the passage's past-tense narration of a historical movement.

• Option 3: "believes" is present tense, which does not match the past-tense verbs used throughout the rest of the passage.

NOTE

• When a comprehension passage narrates historical events or movements, always scan the surrounding sentences for the dominant tense (here, Past Simple) and pick the option that matches it — this is one of the most common cloze-test traps in SSC exams.

Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Romantic poetry is a literary movement that emerged in the late 18th century and continued through the mid-19th century. It is (1)________ by an emphasis on emotion, imagination and individualism. Romantic poets sought to express their innermost thoughts and feelings through their poetry, often exploring (2)_______ such as love, beauty and mortality. One of the defining features of Romantic poetry is its use of language and imagery to evoke powerful emotions in the reader. Many Romantic poets, such as William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge (3)_________ that poetry should be written in the language of common people, rather than in the lofty, formal language of the past. They also incorporated vivid descriptions of nature and the natural world into their poetry, using it as a source of inspiration and spiritual renewal. (4)______ important aspect of Romantic poetry is its focus on the individual and the subjective experience. Romantic poets believed that each persons experience of the world was unique and valuable, and sought to capture this individuality in their writing. This led to a greater emphasis on personal expression and introspection in poetry, (5)_______ a rejection of the traditional poetic forms and structures of the past.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Another.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Another important aspect of Romantic poetry is its focus on the individual and the subjective experience." This sentence introduces a new, additional point about Romantic poetry (after nature/imagery were already discussed), so the determiner "Another" (= "one more, of the same kind") is the natural fit before a singular noun phrase like "important aspect".

• Rule: "Another" is used before a singular countable noun to mean "one more of the same kind" — exactly the sense needed to introduce yet one more "aspect" of Romantic poetry after previous aspects have already been described.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Mostly" is an adverb and cannot grammatically modify the noun phrase "important aspect" at the start of the sentence.

• Option 2: "Additional" is an adjective and would need an article before it ("An additional important aspect..."); used alone before "important aspect" it is grammatically incomplete.

• Option 4: "Farther" relates to physical distance ("a farther point"), which is meaningless in this context of listing aspects of a literary movement.

NOTE

• Distinguish: "another" (determiner, = one more of the same kind, used directly before a singular noun) vs. "other/others" (used before plural nouns or standing alone) vs. "the other" (the remaining one of a specific set).

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Romantic poetry is a literary movement that emerged in the late 18th century and continued through the mid-19th century. It is (1)________ by an emphasis on emotion, imagination and individualism. Romantic poets sought to express their innermost thoughts and feelings through their poetry, often exploring (2)_______ such as love, beauty and mortality. One of the defining features of Romantic poetry is its use of language and imagery to evoke powerful emotions in the reader. Many Romantic poets, such as William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge (3)_________ that poetry should be written in the language of common people, rather than in the lofty, formal language of the past. They also incorporated vivid descriptions of nature and the natural world into their poetry, using it as a source of inspiration and spiritual renewal. (4)______ important aspect of Romantic poetry is its focus on the individual and the subjective experience. Romantic poets believed that each persons experience of the world was unique and valuable, and sought to capture this individuality in their writing. This led to a greater emphasis on personal expression and introspection in poetry, (5)_______ a rejection of the traditional poetic forms and structures of the past.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. as well as.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "This led to a greater emphasis on personal expression and introspection in poetry, as well as a rejection of the traditional poetic forms and structures of the past." Here, two consequences ("a greater emphasis on personal expression..." and "a rejection of the traditional poetic forms...") are being added together, not contrasted.

• Rule — Connectors: "As well as" is used to add one item/idea to another of a similar nature (both being positive consequences here), whereas "whereas" and "but" are used to show contrast, and "therefore" is used to show a result/conclusion that follows logically as a separate clause.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "whereas" is a contrast connector; there is no contrast between the two ideas here — both are consequences of the same trend, so "whereas" is inappropriate.

• Option 2: "therefore" would suggest that "a rejection of traditional poetic forms" is a separate conclusion drawn from the first clause, but grammatically it cannot smoothly connect two noun phrases in a single clause like this.

• Option 4: "but" is a contrast connector, which is inappropriate since both ideas support the same overall point about Romantic poetry.

NOTE

• Connector classification for SSC cloze tests: Addition — and, as well as, along with, in addition to; Contrast — but, whereas, however, although; Result — therefore, thus, hence, consequently.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence.
As a punishment for his betrayal to his country, the spy who sold secrets was sent to prison.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Loyalty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "betrayal" means the act of being disloyal or unfaithful to a person, country, or cause; treachery. (विश्वासघात)

◦ Example: His betrayal of his best friend's trust destroyed their relationship.

• The antonym of "betrayal" is "loyalty", which means faithfulness or devotion to a person, cause, or country. (निष्ठा/वफादारी)

◦ Example: The soldier's loyalty to his country never wavered, even in the most difficult times.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Infidelity" (बेवफाई): Means unfaithfulness, especially to a spouse or partner — this is actually a synonym, not an antonym, of betrayal.

• Option 3: "Perilous" (खतरनाक): Means dangerous or risky; it is an adjective unrelated in meaning to "betrayal" or its opposite.

• Option 4: "Nasty" (गंदा/बुरा): Means unpleasant or unkind; it does not express the opposite of betrayal.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "betrayal": treachery, disloyalty, treason, deceit.

• Other antonyms of "betrayal": faithfulness, allegiance, fidelity, devotion.

• Do not confuse "infidelity" (a synonym of betrayal, meaning disloyalty) with "fidelity" (an antonym, meaning loyalty) — the prefix "in-" reverses the meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Skeptic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Believer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Skeptic" means a person who habitually doubts accepted beliefs or questions the truth of something. (संशयवादी/शंकालु व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: As a skeptic, she refused to accept the salesman's claims without solid proof.

• The antonym of "Skeptic" is "Believer", meaning a person who has faith in or readily accepts something as true. (विश्वास करने वाला व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: He is a firm believer in the power of hard work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Atheist" (नास्तिक): A person who does not believe in the existence of God — this is a specific type of disbeliever, not the general opposite of "skeptic" in the sense of doubt versus belief.

• Option 3: "Careful" (सावधान): Means cautious or attentive; it does not relate to the concept of doubt versus belief.

• Option 4: "Infidel" (काफ़िर): A person who does not follow a particular religion; again a narrower, religion-specific term and not a general antonym of "skeptic".

NOTE

• Related words: skepticism (noun, the attitude of doubt), credulous (too ready to believe, a near-synonym of "believer" in a negative sense), cynic (a person distrustful of others' motives — close to but not identical to "skeptic").

• Do not confuse "atheist" (disbelief in God specifically) with "skeptic" (general doubt about claims).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.
He asked his father when would come the next letter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the next letter would come.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sentence should read: "He asked his father when the next letter would come."

• Rule — Word order in Indirect/Reported Questions: When a question is converted into indirect (reported) speech, or is embedded inside a larger sentence (as here, introduced by "asked...when"), the word order changes from question order (auxiliary + subject) to statement order (subject + auxiliary/verb). The interrogative structure ("would come the next letter") must NOT be retained.

• Applying the rule: the direct question would have been "When would the next letter come?" As an embedded/reported question, the subject "the next letter" must come before the auxiliary "would": "...when the next letter would come."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No substitution required" is incorrect because the original sentence wrongly retains the interrogative (question) word order inside a statement, which is a grammatical error.

• Option 3: "would the next letter come" is incorrect because it still keeps the auxiliary "would" before the subject "the next letter", i.e., question word order, which is not allowed in an embedded question.

• Option 4: "come the next letter" is incorrect because it drops the auxiliary "would" altogether, which is needed to preserve the original modal meaning, and it also keeps the verb before the subject.

NOTE

• This rule applies to all embedded/indirect questions: "I don't know where he lives" (NOT "where does he live"); "She asked what I wanted" (NOT "what did I want").

• The general reported-speech word order is: reporting clause + question word/if/whether + Subject + Verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Last year art critics praised Animesh as if he were a master, but he turned out to be a pleasure for a short time.
option_4: a bull in a china shop
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. a nine days' wonder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a nine days' wonder" means something or someone that creates a great sensation or excitement for a very short time and is then quickly forgotten. (क्षणिक आश्चर्य/अस्थायी सनसनी)

◦ Example: The singer's sudden fame turned out to be a nine days' wonder; nobody remembers him now.

• This exactly matches the sense of "a pleasure for a short time" in the sentence — Animesh was praised as a master but the admiration/sensation lasted only briefly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "a dish fit for Gods" (अत्यंत उत्तम वस्तु): Means something of the very highest quality — unrelated to something being short-lived.

• Option 3: "a house of cards" (कमजोर/अस्थिर योजना): Means a plan, organisation, or structure that is fragile and likely to collapse suddenly — refers to instability, not short-lived fame.

• Option 4: "a bull in a china shop" (उपद्रवी/लापरवाह व्यक्ति): Refers to a clumsy, careless person who causes damage in a delicate situation — unrelated to the idea of brief fame.

NOTE

• Other idioms about short-lived things often asked in SSC: "a flash in the pan" (a brief, one-time success that is not repeated), "a storm in a teacup" (a lot of fuss over something unimportant).

• Do not confuse "a nine days' wonder" (short-lived fame/sensation) with "a flash in the pan" (a one-off success that fails to be repeated) — both relate to brevity but with slightly different shades.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
The professor did an objective evaluation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. unbiased.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "objective" (as used here, as an adjective) means not influenced by personal feelings or opinions; based on facts; impartial. (निष्पक्ष)

◦ Example: The judge gave an objective assessment of the case, uninfluenced by public opinion.

• "Unbiased" carries the same meaning — free from prejudice, showing no favouritism — making it the closest substitute for "objective" in this sentence. (निष्पक्ष/पक्षपातरहित)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "unfair" (अनुचित): Means not fair or just — this is close to the opposite of "objective", not a synonym.

• Option 2: "prejudiced" (पक्षपाती): Means having a preconceived, biased opinion — this is the direct opposite of "objective".

• Option 4: "unjust" (अन्यायपूर्ण): Means not fair or reasonable in treatment — again closer to the opposite of what "objective" conveys.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "objective" (impartial, fact-based) with its opposite "subjective" (based on personal feelings/opinions) — this pair is frequently tested in SSC vocabulary questions.

• Other synonyms of "objective" (as an adjective): impartial, neutral, fair-minded, even-handed.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Comical
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Tragic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Comical" means causing laughter; funny or amusing, especially in an odd or absurd way. (हास्यास्पद/मज़ेदार)

◦ Example: His comical expressions made the entire audience burst into laughter.

• The antonym of "Comical" is "Tragic", meaning causing or expressing great sadness or suffering; deeply distressing. (दुखद/दुखांत)

◦ Example: The play ended on a tragic note, with the hero's untimely death.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Remedial" (उपचारात्मक): Means intended to correct or improve something — unrelated to the humour/sadness spectrum.

• Option 3: "Farcical" (हास्यास्पद/बेतुका): Means ridiculous or absurd, similar in meaning to "comical" — this is actually a near synonym, not an antonym.

• Option 4: "Rebellious" (विद्रोही): Means showing a desire to resist authority — unrelated in meaning to "comical".

NOTE

• Literary genre pair frequently tested: comedy vs. tragedy; comical/comic (adj. of comedy) vs. tragic (adj. of tragedy).

• Other synonyms of "comical": funny, hilarious, ludicrous, farcical, laughable.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The bride had a big villa in comparison to the bridegroom's _____ house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. small.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence sets up an explicit comparison using the phrase "in comparison to", contrasting the bride's "big villa" with the bridegroom's house. Logically, for a meaningful comparison to be drawn, the bridegroom's house must be described with a word that contrasts with "big" — that is, "small".

• Rule — Contextual word choice in comparisons: When a sentence explicitly signals a comparison or contrast ("in comparison to", "whereas", "while", "but"), the blank must be filled with a word whose meaning is logically consistent with — usually opposite to — the quality already mentioned, to make the sentence meaningful.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "large" is inconsistent because it repeats the same idea as "big villa" instead of contrasting with it, making the comparison pointless.

• Option 3: "distinct" means clearly different or separate, but it does not specifically indicate size, so it fails to create the size-based contrast the sentence demands.

• Option 4: "different" is too vague — it does not specify how the bridegroom's house differs in size from the bride's villa, so the comparison remains incomplete.

NOTE

• Watch for comparison/contrast signal words in SSC fill-in-the-blank questions — "in comparison to", "compared with", "whereas", "unlike" — they usually require an option that is opposite in sense to a quality already stated in the sentence.

• Common size-contrast pairs tested: big/small, large/tiny, huge/little, vast/compact.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mantain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The incorrect spelling is "Mantain"; the correct spelling is "Maintain" — to keep something in an existing state, or to continue an activity.

• Spelling key: MAIN + TAIN. The word begins with "main" (as in the everyday word "main"), followed by "tain". In "Mantain", the letter "i" after "Ma" has been wrongly dropped.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Aquarium" is correctly spelt — a tank or container in which fish and other aquatic creatures are kept.

• Option 3: "Accurate" is correctly spelt — precise and exact, free from errors.

• Option 4: "Excellence" is correctly spelt — the quality of being outstanding or extremely good.

NOTE

• Related words to "maintain": maintenance (noun), maintainable (adjective) — all retain the "main" root.

• Other commonly misspelt words in SSC exams: "occurrence", "questionnaire", "necessary", "definitely", "embarrass" — always check for doubled/single consonants and silent letters.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
bread and butter
option_1: An activity you do to get help others
option_2: An activity you do with determination
option_3: An activity you do to improve your culinary skills
option_4: An activity you do to get money for basic needs
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An activity you do to get money for basic needs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bread and butter" means one's main source of income; the job or activity that provides the money needed for basic living expenses. (जीविका/रोज़ी-रोटी)

◦ Example: Teaching is his bread and butter, though he paints as a hobby in his free time.

• The idiom draws on "bread and butter" as the most basic, essential food, symbolising the fundamental means of survival/livelihood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "An activity you do to get help others" does not match the idiom's meaning; the idiom refers to earning a livelihood, not helping others.

• Option 2: "An activity you do with determination" describes the manner of doing something, not the idea of a livelihood, so it does not fit.

• Option 3: "An activity you do to improve your culinary skills" wrongly takes "bread and butter" literally as being about cooking/food skills, rather than its idiomatic sense of a livelihood.

NOTE

• Other food-related idioms of livelihood/importance often asked in SSC: "earn one's bread" (to earn a living), "the biggest slice of the cake" (the largest share of something desirable).

• "Bread and butter" can also be used as an adjective, e.g., "bread-and-butter issues" meaning basic, everyday concerns (as opposed to abstract ones).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the following sentence.
If you do hard work, you will have the expected results.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. desired results.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "expected" means regarded as likely to happen or looked forward to as a hoped-for outcome. (अपेक्षित/वांछित)

◦ Example: After months of preparation, she finally achieved the expected results in her exam.

• "Desired" means wanted or wished for, which closely matches the sense of "expected" (i.e., results that one is hoping/looking forward to) in this context. (वांछित/इच्छित)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "good results" is too general — "expected" specifically refers to results that were anticipated/hoped for, not merely results that are "good".

• Option 2: "required results" shifts the meaning to results that are "necessary" or "mandatory", which is not the same as results one "expects" or hopes for.

• Option 4: "bad results" is the opposite of the intended meaning and contradicts the positive tone of the sentence ("if you do hard work...").

NOTE

• Distinguish close synonyms: "expected" (anticipated), "desired" (wanted), "required" (necessary/mandatory) — SSC vocabulary questions often test such fine shades of meaning among near-synonyms.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
Although I have a lot of work to do, I am determined to finish it all by the end of the day so that I can enjoy my weekend not having any imminent due dates.
option_2: not with any pressure of due date
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. without any looming deadlines.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "not having any imminent due dates" means not having any deadlines that are about to arrive very soon. "Imminent" means about to happen very soon, and a "due date" is a deadline. (आसन्न समय-सीमा न होना)

• "Without any looming deadlines" conveys the same idea precisely — "looming" means about to happen soon, in a way that feels close or threatening, which is an accurate paraphrase of "imminent", and "deadlines" correctly paraphrases "due dates".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "not with any pressure of due date" is awkward and grammatically unnatural English, and shifts the focus to "pressure" rather than the existence of upcoming due dates themselves.

• Option 3: "with no pending reservations" wrongly introduces the idea of "reservations" (as in bookings), which is unrelated to deadlines/due dates.

• Option 4: "not leaving any work incomplete" changes the meaning — the original phrase is about the absence of near-term deadlines, not about completing all work.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "imminent": impending, looming, approaching, forthcoming.

• Do not confuse "imminent" (about to happen soon) with "eminent" (famous/distinguished) — this pair is a classic SSC spelling/meaning trap.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
Her voice, soft and _________, (shrill) flowed effortlessly through the room.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. mellow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "shrill" means (of a sound) high-pitched and piercing; sharp and harsh. (कर्कश/तीखी आवाज़)

◦ Example: The shrill whistle of the referee stopped the match instantly.

• The antonym of "shrill" is "mellow", meaning (of a sound) pleasantly smooth and soft; not harsh. (मधुर/कोमल)

◦ Example: The mellow tone of the old singer's voice soothed the entire audience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "nasal" (नाक से निकलने वाली आवाज़): Describes a sound produced through the nose — it is a description of vocal quality, not the opposite of "shrill".

• Option 3: "croaky" (कर्कश/भारी आवाज़): Means a harsh, hoarse voice (like a frog's croak) — this is close in unpleasantness to "shrill", not its opposite.

• Option 4: "piercing" (तीक्ष्ण/भेदने वाली): Is actually a near-synonym of "shrill" (a piercing sound is sharp and high-pitched), not an antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "shrill": piercing, sharp, screeching, high-pitched.

• Other antonyms of "shrill": soft, soothing, mellow, dulcet.

question:
Identify the incorrectly spelt word and select its correct spelling.
It is his previlage to present all the candidates for ordination to the bishop of the diocese.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. privilege.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The incorrectly spelt word in the sentence is "previlage"; the correct spelling is "privilege" — a special right, advantage, or immunity granted to a particular person or group.

• Spelling key: PRIVI + LEGE. Note the sequence "i" (not "e") after "priv-", and the ending "-lege" (not "-lage"). The word is unrelated to "village" despite the similar-sounding ending, so the "-lage" spelling in the options is a common trap.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "deocease" is not the correct spelling of any word in the sentence; the word actually used is "diocese" (a district under the authority of a bishop), which is correctly spelt in the original sentence.

• Option 3: "prevalage" is not a valid alternative; it does not correctly represent the word "privilege" either.

• Option 4: "odination" is not the correct spelling of the word "ordination" (the act of conferring holy orders on someone), which is correctly spelt in the original sentence.

NOTE

• Related words: privileged (adjective), underprivileged (adjective, lacking normal privileges).

• Other commonly misspelt words with the "-ege"/"-age" confusion: college, sacrilege, allege — always double-check the ending against "-lage", a frequent wrong spelling.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Planets in our solar system close and big for them to twinkle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. are too close and big.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sentence should read: "Planets in our solar system are too close and big for them to twinkle."

• Rule — "too...for...to" construction: The structure "too + adjective + for + object + to + verb" is used to show that something possesses a quality to such an excessive degree that a particular result cannot happen. Here, planets are "too close and big" — to such a degree that the result "for them to twinkle" cannot occur.

• Additionally, the subject "Planets" is plural, so the verb must agree with it as "are", not "is".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "is close and big" is incorrect on two counts: the singular verb "is" does not agree with the plural subject "Planets", and it omits "too", so the "for...to" clause no longer makes logical sense.

• Option 2: "are quite close and big" correctly fixes the subject-verb agreement, but "quite" does not create the necessary "excessive degree" meaning needed to logically connect with "for them to twinkle" (not twinkling).

• Option 4: "very close and big" also fails to supply "too" before the adjectives, and further drops the auxiliary verb "are" altogether, making the sentence ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Contrast: "too" + adjective + to-infinitive (negative/undesirable result, e.g., "too big to fit") versus "so" + adjective + that-clause (e.g., "so big that it did not fit") versus "enough" (placed after the adjective, e.g., "big enough to fit", positive/possible result).

• Subject-verb agreement with plural nouns like "planets", "stars", "students" always requires "are/were", not "is/was".

question: Which of the following sentences contains the ANTONYM of the word 'ignore'?
option_1: Avoid foods which make you sick.
option_2: He did not succeed in gaining custody of his daughter.
option_3: Ritika recognised Kavita in the gathering.
option_4: To keep a tidy kitchen, do not neglect washing your dishes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ritika recognised Kavita in the gathering.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "ignore" means to deliberately take no notice of someone or something; to fail to acknowledge. (अनदेखा करना/नज़रअंदाज़ करना)

◦ Example: He ignored the warning signs and kept driving through the storm.

• The antonym of "ignore" is "recognise", meaning to identify or acknowledge someone/something; to take notice of. (पहचानना/स्वीकार करना)

• In option 3, the word "recognised" is used ("Ritika recognised Kavita in the gathering"), which directly expresses the opposite of ignoring — Ritika noticed and acknowledged Kavita.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Avoid foods which make you sick." contains "avoid", which is close in meaning to "ignore/keep away from", not its opposite.

• Option 2: "He did not succeed in gaining custody of his daughter." does not contain any word related to noticing or acknowledging; it is about failing to gain legal custody.

• Option 4: "To keep a tidy kitchen, do not neglect washing your dishes." contains "neglect", which is a near-synonym of "ignore" (to fail to attend to something), not its antonym — the negative "do not neglect" implies attending to it, but the tested word "neglect" itself is a synonym, not the antonym, of "ignore".

NOTE

• Synonyms of "ignore": neglect, overlook, disregard, snub.

• Antonyms of "ignore": notice, recognise, acknowledge, heed.

• Such "which sentence contains the antonym" questions require scanning each sentence for the one word whose core meaning is opposite to the given word, not just sentences with a similar overall idea.

question:
Select the most appropriate connotation to fill in the blank.
Raju is such a _________always prying into other people's business!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. nosy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes someone who is "always prying into other people's business" — that is, someone who is excessively curious about matters that do not concern them.

• The word "nosy" means excessively curious about other people's affairs; prying. (दूसरों के मामलों में दखल देने वाला) This exactly matches the description given in the sentence.

◦ Example: The nosy neighbour was always peeking through the curtains to see what everyone was doing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "cheeky" (ढीठ/गुस्ताख़): Means impudent or disrespectful in a bold, often light-hearted way — unrelated to prying into others' affairs.

• Option 2: "stingy" (कंजूस): Means unwilling to spend or give, i.e., miserly — unrelated to curiosity about others' business.

• Option 4: "perky" (फुर्तीला/जोशीला): Means cheerful, lively, and full of energy — unrelated to the idea of prying.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "nosy": prying, inquisitive, meddlesome, snoopy.

• Do not confuse "nosy" (excessively curious about others' affairs) with "curious" (a more neutral word for wanting to know or learn something).
